t: Lesson 14 — Step 12: the case packer, both sizes, and the VFD
html:
In the app

Guided mode’s lesson 14 is this chapter: it checks that the lesson’s tags are made, that S12_Pack exists, is called from MainRoutine and verifies, and then watches the line while you run it and ticks each result as it happens:

  • A case stops under the packer head (Case_In_Place)
  • The drive runs at the creep speed (Case_Speed_Ref 2500 = 15 Hz)
  • A case is packed (Case_Full)
  • A case of small bottles is packed from the lower lane (Case_Small_Count)
  • A case of large bottles is packed from the deck (Case_Large_Count)
  • STOP on Pack_HMI stops the packer and START runs it again (Pack_Run)
  • A packed case leaves at Case_Out

The last station packs the finished bottles. A top-load case packer stands at the end of the main line with two lanes to pick from. The large bottles that reach the end of the deck go into its deck infeed (it holds eight). The small bottles come down the divert conveyor on the floor to its lower lane. On a rising edge of Pack_Drop the pick head takes four from one lane, lifts them across to the case lane beside the line and lowers them into the case standing under the head; from the lower lane the head first runs out over the floor conveyor and drops the full 1.7 m to the bottle tops. One size per case: the program chooses the lane, and every case is either four large or four small. The case lane is the other new thing in this lesson. Its motor is not switched by a contactor like every other conveyor on the line: it runs on a variable frequency drive, and the program tells the drive how fast through an analog output.

How the drive is wired

This is how most drives are wired to a CompactLogix. Digital outputs: Case_Run (two-wire: the drive runs while it is 1) and Case_VFD_Reset. One analog output, the speed reference: a 0–10 V signal from channel 0 of the 1769-OF4 to the drive’s analog input, which the drive reads as 0–60 Hz. Digital inputs back: Case_VFD_Ready, Case_VFD_Running (output frequency above zero, also while it slows down), Case_At_Speed and Case_VFD_Fault; and one analog input, the drive’s output frequency, 0–10 V for 0–60 Hz.

The analog channels are in engineering units: the number in the tag is millivolts, 0–10000 for 0–10.000 V. So the program cannot write “15 Hz” to the drive; it writes the voltage that the drive will read as 15 Hz: 15 ÷ 60 × 10000 = 2500. That conversion is the whole of analog output, and SCP (chapter 8) does it.

Why a creep speed

A drive does not stop when Run drops: it ramps down on its decel time, 0.5 s from 60 Hz to 0 on this one. The case lane runs at 150 px/s at 60 Hz, so a case told to stop at full speed travels on for about 37 px, and the packer’s case-in-place window is ±6 px. The cure every packaging line uses: a slow-down eye a little before the mark (Case_Slow, 100 px before the head), a creep speed from there (15 Hz), and the stop on the mark. From 15 Hz the drive is down in an eighth of a second and the case stops within about 2 px.

Add the JSR under step 11 and write:

The rungs

How it fits together

Rungs 0–1 give the packer a run seal-in of its own: a one-scan Pack_Auto_Start when the line starts, so the console’s Start starts the packer too, and a seal-in on Pack_Run that START and STOP on Pack_HMI also work. Stop the packer while the line runs and its lanes fill; when the deck infeed is full, step 11’s bit 7 stops the line. Stop the line and the packer keeps packing what is waiting.

Rungs 2–4 come first, because without them nothing on the case lane moves: the drive runs at whatever its speed reference says, and that is 0 until the program writes one. Rung 2 sets the fast speed, 60 Hz, whenever the case is not creeping. Rung 3 is the analog output: SCP maps 0–60 Hz onto 0–10000. Rung 4 is the same instruction the other way round: the drive’s output frequency back to Hz in a REAL, so you can watch the ramps in Monitor Tags.

Rung 5 runs the lane whenever no empty case stands under the head: either nothing is in place (bring the next case in) or the case in place is full (carry it out). Rungs 6–7 are the creep, latched: the slow-down eye only sees the case going past it, and the case still has 60 px to go when the eye clears. An empty case under the head ends the creep. Rung 8 is the creep speed, 15 Hz, while the latch is on.

Rung 9 chooses the lane. The packer reads its Pick_Lower output on the rising edge of Drop: 1 picks from the lower lane, 0 from the deck. If only the lower lane is ready, it is chosen; if both are, GEQ(Lower_Count,Infeed_Count) takes the fuller lane, so neither lane backs up while the other is served. Rung 10 packs: the packer running, a case worth in a lane, an empty case on the mark, the head home, and the lane stopped. XIO(Case_VFD_Running), not XIO(Case_Run): Run drops the moment the case is in place, but the drive is still ramping down for a few scans, and a head that comes down on a moving case misses it. Rung 11 counts the case by size for Pack_HMI, rung 12 lets Enter clear the counts with the others, and rung 13 sends Reset to the drive’s fault reset: a drive clears a trip only on that rising edge, and only once the cause has gone.

Run it

Start the line and put Case_Hz, Case_Speed_Ref, Case_Hz_Actual, Case_In_Place and Infeed_Count in Quick Watch. The first carton comes in at 60 Hz (Case_Speed_Ref 10000), reaches the slow-down eye, drops to 2500 and creeps, and stops under the head. Bottles collect in both lanes; when one lane holds four, the head picks them and lowers them into the case, goes home empty, and the case leaves with four bottle tops showing. CASES counts 1, and CASES LARGE or CASES SMALL on Pack_HMI.

Watch for: the stop that is not a stop

Take the creep out (or set it to 60 Hz) and run: the case reaches the mark, Run drops, and the case sails on 30-odd px on the decel ramp, out of the window; case-in-place goes back to 0, the lane runs again, and the case leaves empty. Nothing in the program is wrong except the physics. Every positioning problem with a drive is this one: the stopping distance is speed × decel time ÷ 2.

Try it

Press STOP on Pack_HMI while the line runs: the head finishes its cycle and stops, the lower lane fills and the divert conveyor stops at LS12, the deck infeed fills and bit 7 stops the line. Press START, Reset, Start, and watch both lanes drain. Set the creep to 30 Hz (5000) and count how often the case still lands in the window. Then inject a drive trip on Case_VFD: bit 6 latches, the lane coasts to a stop, the infeed fills, and at eight bit 7 stops the line. Clear Machine Faults, Reset, and watch the drive come back.

rungs.head: S12_Pack · Rung 0
rungs.comment: PACKER AUTO-START: one scan when the line starts, so the console Start starts the packer too
rungs.words: When Line_Run (Seal-in run bit (LogixPro B3:0/0)) is on and this is the first scan of it, the rung turns Pack_Auto_Start (One scan when the line starts: starts the packer too) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Line_Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Line_Run is on.
  2. ONS(Pack_Line_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in Pack_Line_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  3. OTE(Pack_Auto_Start) Output Energize does: turns Pack_Auto_Start on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.
pats.think: a turnstile. However long you stand in it, it counts you once.
pats.watch: Each one-shot needs its own storage bit. Two one-shots sharing a bit fight over it, and one of them never fires.

rungs.head: S12_Pack · Rung 1
rungs.comment: PACKER RUN: a seal-in of its own. START and STOP on Pack_HMI pulse Pack_Start and Pack_Stop, so the packer can be stopped while the line runs (its lanes fill and step 11 stops the line at Infeed_Full) and keeps packing after the line stops

pred.q: Pack_Start is on, Pack_Auto_Start is off, Pack_Run is off and Pack_Stop is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Pack_Run is on.

rungs.words: When either (Pack_Start (START on Pack_HMI (pulsed by the touch screen)) is on), (Pack_Auto_Start (One scan when the line starts: starts the packer too) is on) or (Pack_Run (The packer is running (its own seal-in)) is on) and Pack_Stop (STOP on Pack_HMI (pulsed by the touch screen)) is off, the rung turns Pack_Run on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 3 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Pack_Start) Examine If Closed asks: true when Pack_Start is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Pack_Auto_Start) Examine If Closed asks: true when Pack_Auto_Start is on.
    Path 3
    1. XIC(Pack_Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Pack_Run is on.
  2. XIO(Pack_Stop) Examine If Open asks: true when Pack_Stop is off.
  3. OTE(Pack_Run) Output Energize does: turns Pack_Run on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

pats.why: The start condition turns Pack_Run on, and Pack_Run’s own contact in the parallel path keeps the rung true after the start goes away. Anything in series outside the branch (a stop, a fault) breaks it, and then it stays off until the start is made again.
pats.think: a doorbell button and a hand. The start button is the doorbell, pressed for a moment. The seal-in contact is a hand that grabs the circuit as soon as the output comes on and keeps holding after you let go. The stop button, in series, is the only thing that can knock that hand away.
pats.watch: The stop has to be in series outside the branch. Put it inside the start path only and the seal-in path bypasses it: the stop no longer stops.

rungs.head: S12_Pack · Rung 2
rungs.comment: DRIVE SPEED FIRST, or the case lane has no speed reference and nothing moves. FAST: 60 Hz while not creeping

pred.q: Case_Creep is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Case_Hz is not written (it keeps its value). It stops at XIO(Case_Creep).

rungs.words: When Case_Creep (Latched from the slow-down eye until an empty case stands under the head) is off, the rung puts 60 into Case_Hz (Case lane speed the program wants, in Hz).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIO(Case_Creep) Examine If Open asks: true when Case_Creep is off.
  2. MOV(60,Case_Hz) Move does: puts 60 into Case_Hz. It writes every scan the rung is true.

rungs.head: S12_Pack · Rung 3
rungs.comment: SCALE Hz to the analog output: 0-60 Hz is 0-10 V, and the channel counts 0-10000 for 0-10.000 V. 15 Hz goes out as 2500
rungs.words: Every scan, the rung scales Case_Hz (Case lane speed the program wants, in Hz) from 0…60 to 0…10000 into Case_Speed_Ref (Case lane drive speed reference: 0-10000 = 0-10 V = 0-60 Hz).
rungs.ltr: 1. SCP(Case_Hz,0,60,0,10000,Case_Speed_Ref) Scale with Parameters does: scales Case_Hz from 0…60 to 0…10000 into Case_Speed_Ref.

pats.why: A raw number from a module (counts) is turned into engineering units, or the other way, with a straight line between two points.
pats.think: converting a thermometer’s millimetres of mercury into degrees: two marks on the glass are enough to read every other point.

rungs.head: S12_Pack · Rung 4
rungs.comment: READ BACK the drive's own analog output (output frequency, 0-10 V) as Hz, to watch the ramps in Monitor Tags
rungs.words: Every scan, the rung scales Case_Hz_Fbk (Case lane drive output frequency: 0-10000 = 0-10 V = 0-60 Hz) from 0…10000 to 0…60 into Case_Hz_Actual (Case lane drive output frequency read back, in Hz).
rungs.ltr: 1. SCP(Case_Hz_Fbk,0,10000,0,60,Case_Hz_Actual) Scale with Parameters does: scales Case_Hz_Fbk from 0…10000 to 0…60 into Case_Hz_Actual.

pats.why: A raw number from a module (counts) is turned into engineering units, or the other way, with a straight line between two points.

rungs.head: S12_Pack · Rung 5
rungs.comment: RUN THE CASE LANE while no empty case stands under the head: bring the next one in, or carry a packed one out. After the line stops it keeps going while either lane holds a case worth
rungs.words: When Pack_Run (The packer is running (its own seal-in)) is on, either (Line_Run (Seal-in run bit (LogixPro B3:0/0)) is on), (Group_Ready (The packer infeed holds a case worth (4)) is on) or (Lower_Ready (The packer lower lane holds a case worth (4 small bottles)) is on) and either (Case_In_Place (A case is centred under the packer head) is off) or (Case_Full (The case under the head has been packed) is on), the rung turns Case_Run (Case lane drive: run (two-wire)) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Pack_Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Pack_Run is on.
  2. A branch of 3 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Line_Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Line_Run is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Group_Ready) Examine If Closed asks: true when Group_Ready is on.
    Path 3
    1. XIC(Lower_Ready) Examine If Closed asks: true when Lower_Ready is on.
  3. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIO(Case_In_Place) Examine If Open asks: true when Case_In_Place is off.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Case_Full) Examine If Closed asks: true when Case_Full is on.
  4. OTE(Case_Run) Output Energize does: turns Case_Run on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: S12_Pack · Rung 6
rungs.comment: CREEP from the slow-down eye, 100 px before the head, until the case stops under it. Latched, because the eye only sees the case going past. Also while a packed case leaves: the next case may already be queued past the eye

pred.q: Case_Slow is on and Case_Full is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Case_Creep latches on.

rungs.words: When either (Case_Slow (Slow-down eye on the case lane, 100 px before the packer head) is on) or (Case_Full (The case under the head has been packed) is on), the rung latches Case_Creep (Latched from the slow-down eye until an empty case stands under the head) on.
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Case_Slow) Examine If Closed asks: true when Case_Slow is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Case_Full) Examine If Closed asks: true when Case_Full is on.
  2. OTL(Case_Creep) Output Latch does: latches Case_Creep on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Case_Creep stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.
pats.think: a light switch rather than a doorbell: flick it on and it stays on until someone flicks it off.
pats.watch: A latched bit survives a stop, and it survives a download that keeps tag values. If nothing ever unlatches it, the machine remembers a state that is long gone.

rungs.head: S12_Pack · Rung 7
rungs.comment: An empty case under the head: stop creeping (the case lane rung has already stopped the lane)
rungs.words: When Case_In_Place (A case is centred under the packer head) is on and Case_Full (The case under the head has been packed) is off, the rung unlatches Case_Creep (Latched from the slow-down eye until an empty case stands under the head).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Case_In_Place) Examine If Closed asks: true when Case_In_Place is on.
  2. XIO(Case_Full) Examine If Open asks: true when Case_Full is off.
  3. OTU(Case_Creep) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Case_Creep. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Case_Creep when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: S12_Pack · Rung 8
rungs.comment: CREEP: 15 Hz, so the case can stop on the mark. From 60 Hz the drive's 0.5 s decel ramp would carry it about 37 px past the head; from 15 Hz, about 2. The SCALE rung above picks it up on the next scan

pred.q: Case_Creep is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Case_Hz is not written (it keeps its value). It stops at XIC(Case_Creep).

rungs.words: When Case_Creep (Latched from the slow-down eye until an empty case stands under the head) is on, the rung puts 15 into Case_Hz (Case lane speed the program wants, in Hz).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Case_Creep) Examine If Closed asks: true when Case_Creep is on.
  2. MOV(15,Case_Hz) Move does: puts 15 into Case_Hz. It writes every scan the rung is true.

rungs.head: S12_Pack · Rung 9
rungs.comment: WHICH LANE: one size per case, so the head picks from whichever lane holds four. With both ready it takes the fuller one (small bottles on a tie), so neither lane backs up. The packer reads Pick_Lower on the rising edge of Drop
rungs.words: When Lower_Ready (The packer lower lane holds a case worth (4 small bottles)) is on and either (Group_Ready (The packer infeed holds a case worth (4)) is off) or (Lower_Count (Small bottles waiting in the packer lower lane) is at least Infeed_Count (Bottles in the packer infeed)), the rung turns Pick_Lower (Packer: the next Drop picks from the lower lane (small bottles) instead of the deck infeed) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Lower_Ready) Examine If Closed asks: true when Lower_Ready is on.
  2. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIO(Group_Ready) Examine If Open asks: true when Group_Ready is off.
    Path 2
    1. GEQ(Lower_Count,Infeed_Count) Greater Than or Equal asks: true when Lower_Count is at least Infeed_Count.
  3. OTE(Pick_Lower) Output Energize does: turns Pick_Lower on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: S12_Pack · Rung 10
rungs.comment: PACK: four bottles in either lane, an empty case centred under the head and the lane stopped (Running is still 1 while the drive decelerates), head home: one rising edge on Drop. The head drops back to its home position empty: the four stay in the case
rungs.words: When Pack_Run (The packer is running (its own seal-in)) is on, either (Group_Ready (The packer infeed holds a case worth (4)) is on) or (Lower_Ready (The packer lower lane holds a case worth (4 small bottles)) is on), Case_In_Place (A case is centred under the packer head) is on, Case_Full (The case under the head has been packed) is off, Case_VFD_Running (Case lane drive output frequency above zero) is off, Packer_Ready (Packer head home, not cycling) is on and this is the first scan of it, the rung turns Pack_Drop (Packer: pick a case worth from the infeed and place it in the case (rising edge)) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Pack_Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Pack_Run is on.
  2. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Group_Ready) Examine If Closed asks: true when Group_Ready is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Lower_Ready) Examine If Closed asks: true when Lower_Ready is on.
  3. XIC(Case_In_Place) Examine If Closed asks: true when Case_In_Place is on.
  4. XIO(Case_Full) Examine If Open asks: true when Case_Full is off.
  5. XIO(Case_VFD_Running) Examine If Open asks: true when Case_VFD_Running is off.
  6. XIC(Packer_Ready) Examine If Closed asks: true when Packer_Ready is on.
  7. ONS(Drop_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in Drop_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  8. OTE(Pack_Drop) Output Energize does: turns Pack_Drop on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.

rungs.head: S12_Pack · Rung 11
rungs.comment: CASES: one count each time a case is packed, on the CASES display, and split by size for CASES LARGE and CASES SMALL on Pack_HMI. Case_Small says which lane filled the case under the head
rungs.words: When Case_Full (The case under the head has been packed) is on and this is the first scan of it, each path is tested on its own: it makes Case_Count (Cases packed, shown on the CASES display) = Case_Count + 1; if Case_Small (The packed case under the head holds small bottles) is on, it makes Case_Small_Count (Cases of small bottles packed (CASES SMALL on Pack_HMI)) = Case_Small_Count + 1; if Case_Small is off, it makes Case_Large_Count (Cases of large bottles packed (CASES LARGE on Pack_HMI)) = Case_Large_Count + 1.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Case_Full) Examine If Closed asks: true when Case_Full is on.
  2. ONS(Case_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in Case_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  3. A branch of 3 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. ADD(Case_Count,1,Case_Count) Add does: makes Case_Count = Case_Count + 1. Every scan the rung is true; behind a one-shot it adds once per event.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Case_Small) Examine If Closed asks: true when Case_Small is on.
    2. ADD(Case_Small_Count,1,Case_Small_Count) Add does: makes Case_Small_Count = Case_Small_Count + 1. Every scan the rung is true; behind a one-shot it adds once per event.
    Path 3
    1. XIO(Case_Small) Examine If Open asks: true when Case_Small is off.
    2. ADD(Case_Large_Count,1,Case_Large_Count) Add does: makes Case_Large_Count = Case_Large_Count + 1. Every scan the rung is true; behind a one-shot it adds once per event.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.

rungs.head: S12_Pack · Rung 12
rungs.comment: Enter on the thumbwheel clears the case counts with the others (step 9)

pred.q: Enter is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Case_Count is written, Case_Large_Count is written and Case_Small_Count is written.

rungs.words: When Enter (Thumbwheel Enter button) is on, the rung clears Case_Count (Cases packed, shown on the CASES display) to 0, clears Case_Large_Count (Cases of large bottles packed (CASES LARGE on Pack_HMI)) to 0 and clears Case_Small_Count (Cases of small bottles packed (CASES SMALL on Pack_HMI)) to 0.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Enter) Examine If Closed asks: true when Enter is on.
  2. A branch of 3 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. CLR(Case_Count) Clear does: clears Case_Count to 0.
    Path 2
    1. CLR(Case_Large_Count) Clear does: clears Case_Large_Count to 0.
    Path 3
    1. CLR(Case_Small_Count) Clear does: clears Case_Small_Count to 0.

rungs.head: S12_Pack · Rung 13
rungs.comment: DRIVE RESET: Reset on the console also pulses the drive's FaultReset. A drive only clears a trip once its cause has gone
rungs.words: When Reset_PB (Blue Reset button: acknowledge alarms and clear the ones whose cause is gone) is on, the rung turns Case_VFD_Reset (Case lane drive: fault reset (rising edge)) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Reset_PB) Examine If Closed asks: true when Reset_PB is on.
  2. OTE(Case_VFD_Reset) Output Energize does: turns Case_VFD_Reset on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

Pack_Auto_Start.desc: One scan when the line starts: starts the packer too

Pack_Start.desc: START on Pack_HMI (pulsed by the touch screen)

Pack_Run.desc: The packer is running (its own seal-in)

Pack_Stop.desc: STOP on Pack_HMI (pulsed by the touch screen)

Case_Creep.desc: Latched from the slow-down eye until an empty case stands under the head

Case_Hz.desc: Case lane speed the program wants, in Hz

Case_Speed_Ref.desc: Case lane drive speed reference: 0-10000 = 0-10 V = 0-60 Hz

Case_Hz_Fbk.desc: Case lane drive output frequency: 0-10000 = 0-10 V = 0-60 Hz

Case_Hz_Actual.desc: Case lane drive output frequency read back, in Hz

Group_Ready.desc: The packer infeed holds a case worth (4)

Lower_Ready.desc: The packer lower lane holds a case worth (4 small bottles)

Case_In_Place.desc: A case is centred under the packer head

Case_Full.desc: The case under the head has been packed

Case_Slow.desc: Slow-down eye on the case lane, 100 px before the packer head

Lower_Count.desc: Small bottles waiting in the packer lower lane

Pick_Lower.desc: Packer: the next Drop picks from the lower lane (small bottles) instead of the deck infeed

Case_VFD_Running.desc: Case lane drive output frequency above zero

Pack_Drop.desc: Packer: pick a case worth from the infeed and place it in the case (rising edge)

Case_Count.desc: Cases packed, shown on the CASES display

Case_Small.desc: The packed case under the head holds small bottles

Case_Small_Count.desc: Cases of small bottles packed (CASES SMALL on Pack_HMI)

Case_Large_Count.desc: Cases of large bottles packed (CASES LARGE on Pack_HMI)

Reset_PB.desc: Blue Reset button: acknowledge alarms and clear the ones whose cause is gone

Case_VFD_Reset.desc: Case lane drive: fault reset (rising edge)
